method: Manual adversarial construct-level review of each candidate against its highest-similarity canonical item after whole-bank zero-trust screening.

comparisons.reason: Both use inner-mitochondrial-membrane transport as a frame, but Q1617 tests SLC25A13/citrin aspartate-glutamate exchange for urea-cycle substrate delivery, whereas Q1631 tests SLC25A3 inorganic-phosphate import required for ATP synthesis. Substrate, transporter, pathway, phenotype, and causal consequence differ.

Q1272 tests neuronal KCC2 chloride extrusion and GABA-A signaling. Q1632 tests PNKP DNA-end chemistry with 5-prime kinase and 3-prime phosphatase activities. Shared seizure phenotype does not constitute mechanistic duplication.

Q1617 tests mitochondrial metabolite exchange by citrin. Q1633 tests ATP13A2-mediated lysosomal polyamine, especially spermine, export. Organelle, substrate, transporter family, disease phenotype, and mechanism are distinct.

Q1216 tests COQ8A-related coenzyme-Q biosynthesis and oxidative phosphorylation. Q1634 tests DDHD2 intracellular triglyceride hydrolysis and neuronal lipid-droplet accumulation. Both can cause neurologic disease, but the biochemical constructs are unrelated.

Q1629 tests LRPPRC-dependent mitochondrial mRNA stabilization/polyadenylation. Q1635 tests MTFMT-dependent formylation of mitochondrial Met-tRNA for translation initiation. Both affect mitochondrial gene expression, but one is mRNA homeostasis and the other is initiator-tRNA modification.
